ds: Fraud against public bodies and large buyers includes bid rigging, inflated invoices, fictitious suppliers and false benefit claims. Collusion between suppliers and officials is a recurring pattern.

src.t: OECD, Guidelines for Fighting Bid Rigging in Public Procurement (2009, rev. 2025)
UK Government Counter Fraud Function, Public Sector Fraud Authority publications
ACFE, Occupational Fraud 2024: A Report to the Nations (2024)

rat: Fraud against public bodies and large buyers via bid rigging, fictitious suppliers and false benefit claims; officials collude with suppliers; payments flow through procurement/purchasing.

ind.n: Tenders show suspiciously similar pricing or documents
ind.cx: Bids contain shared errors, formatting or pricing relationships.
ind.ds: Bids contain shared errors, formatting or pricing relationships.

ind.cx: Contracts win in turn across a small group.
ind.ds: Contracts win in turn across a small group.

ind.cx: Series of awards just below tender limits.
ind.ds: Payments, claims or contracts are broken into amounts just under internal authorisation limits.
ind.cn: Payments or claims split to stay below internal approval limits

ind.n: Supplier is shell company with no footprint
ind.cx: Registered address and staff do not match the supply.
ind.ds: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.
ind.cn: Shell entity with no operating footprint

ind.n: Invoices for services or goods not received
ind.cx: Payment is approved without delivery evidence.
ind.ds: Payment is approved without delivery evidence.

ind.n: Official has undisclosed relationship with supplier
ind.cx: Conflict of interest appears from registry or declarations.
ind.ds: Conflict of interest appears from registry or declarations.

ind.n: Benefit claimants share bank accounts or addresses
ind.cx: Many claims route to same accounts or addresses.
ind.ds: Unrelated customers or applicants share the same phone, email, address, device or bank account, including mail drops and shared accommodation.
ind.cn: Multiple customers sharing contact details or addresses

ind.n: Claim details contradict income or residency evidence
ind.ds: Declared income, dependants or circumstances conflict with data held on the customer.
ind.cn: Claim details inconsistent with income, residency or account history

ind.n: Spike in claims via one agent or channel
ind.ds: Unusual surge in accounts or claims originating from one channel, introducer, agent, IP range or device.
ind.cn: Spike in volume via a single channel, agent or source

ctl.ds: Scores claims, links parties, providers and addresses, monitors repeat claims by region or intermediary and verifies payee identity and sanctions exposure before settlement. It uncovers organised and repeat claims fraud.

Tests bidding and award data for rotation, cover bids, price clustering, splitting, variations and exceptions to competition, and requires independent cost and justification review. It detects collusion and corrupt awards.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

ctl.n: Vendor master-data and bank-detail change control
ctl.ds: Requires independent verification and review of any new or changed supplier bank details before the next payment run, including challenge of redirections to third-country accounts. It stops payment-diversion and business-email-compromise fraud.

Confirms the existence of underlying goods, services or receivables directly with the obligor or through inspection before funds are advanced. It defeats fictitious invoices and transactions that exist only on paper.

ctl.n: Segregation of duties and dual authorisation
ctl.ds: Ensures no single person can create, approve and release a payment or master-data change, requiring an independent second approver. It controls insider and impersonation fraud.

Provides protected, confidential channels for staff, workers and suppliers to report misconduct or concerns, together with conduct monitoring to surface insider collusion. It brings internal and supply-chain issues to light.

Requires refunds, cancellations and aborted-deal repayments to go back only to the original payer and method after validation of the request. It blocks the use of refunds to convert illicit funds into clean payments.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Independently verifies stated income, employment, obligations and application facts against third-party, bureau and prior-history data at origination. It reduces application, credit and insurance fraud.
Tracks cases, outcomes, losses and false positives, routes concerns across fraud, sanctions and anti-corruption teams and feeds outcomes into tuning and appetite. It supports consistent handling.
